title: Which orders can the warehouse ship today
examObjective: Applying correct syntax to write DataWeave transformations to coerce, format, order, and filter data
basics: `filter` keeps the elements of an array for which a condition is true and drops the rest. Inside the condition, `$` is the current element. `isEmpty(x)` is true when x is null, an empty String, an empty Array or an empty Object.
prompt:
The warehouse system exports orders as `{ id, status, tracking }`. An order can ship when its `status` is `"packed"` **and** it has a tracking number.

The export is not tidy: some orders have no `tracking` field, and some have `tracking` set to an empty String because the label printer failed. Neither counts as having a tracking number.

Return the `id`s of the orders that can ship, in their original order.
hints: Two conditions, both required. Filter, then take the `id`.
Look at the second hidden shape: `tracking` is there, but it is `""`. Does `!= null` reject it?
`isEmpty` treats null and "" the same way, which is exactly the rule in the task.
solution:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
(payload filter ($.status == "packed" and not isEmpty($.tracking))).id default []

mustFail.why: checks only for null, so an order whose tracking is an empty String gets shipped
mustFail.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
(payload filter ($.status == "packed" and $.tracking != null)).id default []

mustFail.why: uses or instead of and, so any packed order ships whether or not it has tracking
mustFail.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
(payload filter ($.status == "packed" or not isEmpty($.tracking))).id default []

explanation.approach: There are two ways to have no tracking number here: the field is missing (null) or it is an empty String. `isEmpty` covers both. One more detail: selecting `.id` from an empty array gives null, not an empty array, so `default []` keeps the output an array when nothing can ship.

snippets.label: An empty String is not null
snippets.note: A null check lets the failed-label orders through.

snippets.label: isEmpty covers both
snippets.note: The first two are the "no tracking" cases.

snippets.label: Selecting from an empty array
snippets.note: Nothing survives the filter, and a selector on an empty array is null. That is why the solution ends with `default []`.
